sources.title: Yuri I. Ingster, Theofanis Sapatinas and Irina A. Suslina, Minimax signal detection in ill-posed inverse problems
sources.locator: Complete 26-page article. §2, PDF pp. 4–6, error criteria and separation-rate definition; §4.1, PDF pp. 6–7, q=2 extremal problem, weighted chi-square tests, and mixture lower bound; Theorems 4.2–4.5, PDF pp. 12–14, four q=2 regimes; §4.7, Theorem 4.7, PDF pp. 18–19, sparse q<2 regimes and theorem statement.
sources.reading_verification: Inspected the complete 26-page PDF and read the full relevant sections. Section 2 gives the null-first type-I/maximal-type-II risks and both distinguishability limits. Section 4.1 gives the q=2 extremal problem, weighted statistic, and largest-weight qualification for sharp Gaussian errors. The four q=2 rate theorems and the full Theorem 4.7 statement were read. Theorem 4.7 explicitly omits its proof and refers to Ingster–Suslina (2003), Theorems 4.5 and 6.1; no proof was attributed to this article.

contents.name: Minimax detection errors and separation-rate definition
contents.support: Supports the null-first type-I/maximal-type-II convention, total error, separation-rate limits, and Gaussian sharp-error form; the local definition gives the full product-Borel randomized test space.

contents.name: Weighted chi-square extremal statistic and largest-weight condition
contents.locator: §3.1 and §4.1, PDF pp. 6–7, equations (3.1)–(3.3) and Theorem 4.1
contents.support: Supports the finite fourth-power extremal objective, weighted chi-square test, distinguishability parameter, and the qualification that sharp Gaussian errors require the largest weight to vanish; the local proof supplies its own lower and upper arguments.

contents.name: Symmetric Gaussian sign-mixture likelihood ratio
contents.support: Supports the product likelihood ratio and second-moment lower-bound route; the local lemma verifies the finite product law and total-variation constants.

contents.name: Weighted chi-square normal limit

Complete independent special-case proof of the λ=0 q=1, α=β=1 rate by an explicit location/sign mixture lower bound and finite-coordinate maximum test upper bound. It does not prove the univariate general sparse theorem.
